summary: Satya Narayan Goenka worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying under U Ba Khin from around 1955 to 1971. In 1985, he founded the Vipassana Research Institute.

Satya Swarup Misra was an indologist and linguist. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University (~1966-1995).

Satyavrat Shastri was an indologist and linguist who studied at the University of the Punjab and Banaras Hindu University. He held professorial and administrative roles at the University of Delhi (1970-1995) and served as Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya (~1989-1991).

Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Presidency University and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Dhaka (1921-1945), served as physics professor at the University of Calcutta (1945-1956), and was Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956-1958).
Saubhagya Pradhananga works in history, archaeology, and indology. By 2018, Pradhananga served as Chief of the National Archives of Nepal and on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica.

A Buddhist studies figure, Sayadaw U Sīlānanda studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and U Paññāvanta. He was Abbot of Mahavijjodaya Chaung Monastery (1960), Chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (1999), and Founder-abbot of Dhammānanda Vihara (~1993-2005).

Active in Buddhist studies, Sayadaw U Thittila studied under Sayadaw Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University (~1933-1934). He worked as a librarian for the Adyar Library (~1937-1938) and The Buddhist Society (~1938-1944), later lecturing at the University of Rangoon (1952).
Sayaka Sonoda earned a PhD at Toyo University (attested 2015-2016), studying under doctoral supervisor Shinobu Yamaguchi and co-supervisor Shogo Watanabe.

Scott A. Mitchell works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008) and served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).
Scott Dalby works in religious and Buddhist studies, having earned a PhD at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. In 2014, he was attested as a lecturer at Amsterdam University College.
Linguist and Tibetologist Scott DeLancey studied under Yungdrung Manang. He held academic posts at the University of Colorado (~1980-1982) and the University of Oregon (~1982).
Scott Hurley works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under Elizabeth Harrison and completed his PhD at the University of Arizona in 2001.

Scott Pacey works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, completing a doctorate at the Australian National University in 2011. He was a postdoctoral fellow at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Lecturer in Buddhist Thought and Practice at the University of Manchester (attested 2014).
Sean D. Gaffney works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD under Tadeusz Skorupski at SOAS University of London (attested 2003), where he was also attested in a post in 1996.
Sebastian Pole works in Indology and other fields. He completed his studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.
See Mui Yian is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi is a historian and Indologist who earned a doctorate from the University of Cambridge (~1986-1991). She held history posts at Jamia Millia Islamia (~2000-2006), the University of Delhi (~2002-2014), and Ashoka University (~2020).

Seiichi Mizuno specialized in archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees under Kosaku Hamada at Kyoto University. He worked at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities from 1938 and served as a university professor from 1949 to 1968.

Seiichi Yagi works in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, having studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950-1955). He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1968-1989), Kanto Gakuin University, and Toin University of Yokohama.

Seiichiro Ono studied under Eiichi Makino at the University of Tokyo, where he served as an assistant professor and professor (1919-1951). He later held a professorship at Aichi Gakuin University (1957-1977), working in law, Buddhist studies, and philosophy.
